notes: Checked main nav (top-level 'New Arrivals' item), footer ('What's New'), and per-category mega-menu dropdowns. The global page /en-us/new-arrivals is a genuine dedicated New Arrivals PLP: heading 'New Arrivals - Discover what's new', copy 'Did you know our selection is updated weekly with new design products and brands? Here you'll find the latest arrivals gathered in one place - fresh ideas, intriguing new shapes, and details that bring joy to everyday life.' Every per-category mega-menu dropdown (Furniture/Lighting/Kitchen & Dining/Decor/Storage/Bedroom/Bathroom/Outdoor/Lifestyle/For Kids) ALSO carries a 'New arrivals' link, but all of those resolve to '<category>?sort=newest' (e.g. furniture?sort=newest, lighting?sort=newest, decor?sort=newest) - i.e. the ordinary category catalogue page merely re-sorted by newest-first, not a distinct site-defined New Arrivals listing - correctly EXCLUDED per the brief's guidance on arbitrary sort/date-filter pages (same underlying product set as the regular category, already covered by the separate Home-Decor/Furniture project, not a genuine merchandising concept page of its own). The New Arrivals page itself shows category shortcut tiles under 'NEW ARRIVALS FOR EVERY SPACE' (Tableware/Kitchenware/Outdoor/Lighting/Furniture/Decor/Bathroom/Lifestyle & Housekeeping) - these are marketing shortcuts into the same already-excluded per-category '?sort=newest' pages, not genuine separate New-Arrivals sub-listings, so no sub-structure was invented; single undifferentiated row emitted. Count verified via Playwright-rendered DOM text '807 products' directly above the product grid (reproduced identically across two separate page loads). Site is a Vue SPA (per prior Home-Decor pass notes) so SSR HTML carries no count, and the site's own catalog-products JSON API silently falls back to the whole-catalogue total (22917) for unrecognized uris like '/new-arrivals' - the exact trap documented in the prior pass - so DOM text was used instead of that API.
